verdictLine: FIX FIRST (blocking F1, F2): F1, the guard half-converts a symbol pair and is not stable (`(c)(r)` → `(c)®`, then `©®`; before the delta `©®` in one pass), against SPEC.md:172; F2, the new Known limit and changelog promise `501 (c)(3)` keeps its `(c)`, but CKEditor’s as-you-type `copyright` transformation, which Sorts turns on by default, converts it as it is typed. FU1–FU4 are not blocking.

findings.summary: The new lookahead reads a following symbol as a citation, so a symbol pair is half converted on pass 1 and finished only on later passes: `(c)(r)` → `(c)®` (pass 2 `©®`), `(C)(R)` → `(C)®`, `(c)(tm)` → `(c)™`, `Acme (r)(tm) Widget` → `Acme (r)™ Widget`, `(r)(c)` → `(r)©`, `(c)(c)` → `(c)©`, and `(c)(r)(tm)` needs three passes (`(c)(r)™` → `(c)®™` → `©®™`). Before the delta each gave the full symbols in one stable pass (`©®`, `©™`, `®™`, `®©`, `©®™`). This breaks SPEC.md:172 (“running twice equals running once”); fix on save stores the half-converted text while the page pass shows the finished one, and the audit flags the stored value again. README.md:376 says “so `(c)(r)` is left too”, which is not what happens.
findings.location: src/engine/rules/SymbolsRule.php:38 (`(?!\([\p{L}\p{N}]+\))` also matches `(r)`, `(c)`, `(tm)`); README.md:376 (“so `(c)(r)` is left too”)
findings.repro: /opt/homebrew/bin/php <scratch>/gate-s7c3/probe.php src <scratch>/gate-s7c3/inputs.txt en-US → “(c)(r)	=> (c)®	[UNSTABLE 2nd: ©®]”, “(C)(R)	=> (C)®	[UNSTABLE 2nd: ©®]”, “(c)(TM)	=> (c)™	[UNSTABLE 2nd: ©™]”, “Acme (r)(tm) Widget	=> Acme (r)™ Widget	[UNSTABLE 2nd: Acme ®™ Widget]”; inputs2.txt → “(c)(r)(tm)	=> (c)(r)™	[UNSTABLE 2nd: (c)®™]”, “(r)(c)	=> (r)©	[UNSTABLE 2nd: ®©]”. The same in fr, de, en-GB and text mode. On git archive 2d09df2: “(c)(r)	=> ©®”, “(c)(r)(tm)	=> ©®™”, no instability.
findings.acceptance: A `(c)` or `(r)` followed by `(c)`, `(r)` or `(tm)` (any case) converts in one stable pass: `(c)(r)` → `©®`, `(C)(R)` → `©®`, `(c)(tm)` → `©™`, `(r)(tm)` → `®™`, `(r)(c)` → `®©`, `(c)(r)(tm)` → `©®™`, pinned by corpus cases (the corpus runner checks the second pass), while every current citation case still passes; README.md:376 drops “so `(c)(r)` is left too”. A lookahead of `(?!\((?!(?:c|r|tm)\))[\p{L}\p{N}]+\))` does this: in a scratch copy it gives exactly those outputs and the engine suite stays at 5325 passed, 0 failed.
findings.cause: the lookahead treats any parenthesised letters as a citation subsection, including the three symbol spellings the same rule converts, and Run::replaceAll matches every occurrence against the unedited text, so the left (c) sees the (r) that is about to become ®

findings.summary: In a CKEditor field, typing `501 (c)(3)` still gives `501 ©(3)`: Sorts turns on CKEditor’s `copyright` and `registeredTrademark` transformations whenever the symbols rule is on, and CKEditor converts `(c)` the moment the `)` is typed, before `(3)` exists and with no look-behind, so `501(c)(3)` typed attached is converted too (the page pass leaves the attached form alone). The page pass and fix on save cannot restore it. The new Known limit (README.md:376, “A citation such as `501 (c)(3)` keeps its `(c)`”) and CHANGELOG.md:65 promise it without qualification; README.md:256 (“Dashes, ellipsis and symbols follow the rules that are on”) says nothing of it. As-you-type is on by default on Lite and Pro (README.md:172), and the sites most likely to cite 501(c)(3) are non-profits that type into CKEditor.
findings.location: src/ckeditor/CkeditorSupport.php:116–117; craftcms/ckeditor 5.9.0 bundled ckeditor5 TextTransformation (`copyright:{from:`(c)`,to:`©`}`; `normalizeFrom` builds `new RegExp(`(${escapeRegExp(from)})$`)`); README.md:256, :376; CHANGELOG.md:65
findings.repro: Static, from the shipped bundle: grep in vendor/craftcms/ckeditor/src/web/assets/ckeditor/dist/lib/ckeditor5.umd.js.map → “copyright: { from: '(c)', to: '©' }” and “function normalizeFrom( from: string | RegExp ): RegExp { if ( typeof from == 'string' ) { return new RegExp( `(${ escapeRegExp( from ) })$` ); }”; CkeditorSupport::transformations() pushes 'copyright', 'registeredTrademark', 'trademark' when symbols is on. Not observed in a browser (the testbed was not started).
findings.acceptance: Either (a) CkeditorSupport no longer includes `copyright` and `registeredTrademark` (leaving `(c)` and `(r)` to the page pass and fix on save, where the citation guard applies), with its unit test updated and README.md:256 saying so; or (b) the Known limit at README.md:376 and CHANGELOG.md:65 say that text typed in a CKEditor field with as-you-type on is converted as it is typed (`501 (c)(3)` and `501(c)(3)` become `501 ©(3)`), with the way out (switch off as-you-type, or the field’s own `typing` config). Dan’s call which.
findings.cause: the citation guard lives only in the engine; the CKEditor path Sorts configures does the same conversion as you type with CKEditor’s own unguarded pattern, and the new README and CHANGELOG lines do not say so

notBlocking.summary: The docs say “a parenthesised letter or digit”, but the guard takes any run of them, so more than citations is left: `(c)(2026)` and `Copyright (c)(2026) Name` stay as typed (before: `©(2026)`), and so do `Brand (r)(US) only` and `Brand (r)(EU)` (before: `®(US)`, `®(EU)`). Citations with several characters (`(c)(iii)`, `(c)(12)`) are left too, which is right. A year in parentheses right after `(c)` is unusual but is a copyright notice, not a citation.

knownLimits: A `(c)` before a parenthetical that is not a bare run of letters or digits converts, which is right: `Sorts (c)(see notes)` → `Sorts ©(see notes)`, `(c) (2026) Name` → `© (2026) Name` (pinned), `(c)(3` → `©(3`, `(c)()` → `©()`.

A `(c)` and a parenthetical in the next element or paragraph are read apart and convert: `

Sorts (c)
(2026)

` → `©
(2026)`, `

Sorts (c)

(1) next

` → `©`.
The (b)/(q) paragraph rule still applies alongside the guard: `A 501 (c)(3) non-profit (b) list` stays as typed.
confirmedSound: The fix does what its commit says for the shapes it names: `501 (c)(3)`, `501 (C)(3)`, `501 (c)(4)`, `12 (c)(i)`, `(c)(3)` at the start, `Rule 5 (r)(2)`, `§ 501 (c)(3)`, `501 (c)(3)`, `501 (c)(3)(A)`, `26 U.S.C. § 501 (c)(3).` are left; `(c) 2026`, `text (c) more`, `(c) (2026)` still convert. Each new corpus case passes its idempotence pass (suite green).

“12 corpus cases (7 red before)” holds: the new tests/engine at caf694b run against src at 2d09df2 gives “RESULT: 5318 passed, 7 failed”, the seven being the spaced, four-spaced, letter-spaced, upper-spaced, start-of-text, r and then-copyright cases; 5313 + 12 = 5325.

The guard bites: removing the lookahead (M1), digits only (M2), letters only (M3), no opening paren (M6), the guard for (c) only (M8) or for (r) only (M9), and a guard that skips a space (M10) are all killed by the engine suite.
No locale has its own symbol handling (src/engine/locales has no ©, ® or copyright; the rule is locale-free); fr, de and en-GB give the same results as en-US, and text mode the same.
The filter’s escape (src/web/twig/SortsExtension.php:81, ENT_QUOTES) does not touch parentheses, so `"A 501 (c)(3) non-profit"` → `“A 501 (c)(3) non-profit”` and `'501 (c)(3)'` → `‘501 (c)(3)’`.
src/templates/settings.twig:144 (“Symbols: (c) (r) (tm)”) is a label, still accurate; there is no symbols description to update.
